evidence.ref: .warp/executor.py gained an OPTIONAL, default-off run-observer seam (RunObserver base + RunLogObserver reference) so a driven run streams its live loop progress into the R1 run registry: run.started, a step per phase (resolve, plan_check, build, gate, proof, review, merge_ready), a heartbeat while working, a block+resume around the human approve step and a block on the two-failed-review adjudication, and a terminal finish (done with the receipt, or aborted with the reason on a hard halt, never a step past a failed step). A thin warp_run(spec_id, hooks) driver allocates the run via runlog, wires the observer, drives the executor, and returns the receipt plus the run id; the observer is a pure side effect (run() ignores its return values) so an observed and an unobserved run are byte-identical and halt semantics are unchanged; high-volume step/heartbeat stay in the run folder live.jsonl and never reach the committed events.jsonl. plugin/skills/run/SKILL.md notes the front door.

a selftest block drives the instrumented executor over a fake LoopSteps seam and a temp runs root: a success loop writes run.started + a step per phase + run.done; a red-gate halt writes an aborted finish with the reason and no phase past the gate; a human-pause writes a blocked question; the two-failed-review halt blocks (classify blocked) rather than aborting; a crash marks aborted and re-raises; and the DEFAULT-OFF path leaves state/steps/receipt/human_minutes byte-identical with no run folder written; part of selftest 817 passed, 0 failed
